source_headline: Meet the District 6 candidate: With Medicaid cuts looming, how will S.F. keep providing drug treatment and recovery?
angle_statement: San Francisco has set aside $34 million against a Medicaid hole its own health department estimates at $90 million to $180 million a year.
tldr: Supervisor Matt Dorsey says he will work to keep people in drug treatment eligible for Medi-Cal. SF projects losing up to $315 million a year from federal Medicaid cuts.
editor_note: San Francisco has set aside $34 million against a Medicaid hole its own health department estimates at $90 million to $180 million a year. That gap is the story, not the candidate questionnaire it turned up in. Dorsey's answer is to connect people in treatment with jobs so they keep Medi-Cal eligibility, which is a workaround for a work requirement, not a funding plan. Meanwhile the Department of Public Health is already cutting $40 million over two years, including contracts for harm reduction and peer counseling, while the city adds treatment beds and people still wait up to four months for a residential slot. Expanding capacity and cutting the payer at the same time is a decision someone is going to have to name out loud.
what_to_watch: New Medi-Cal eligibility rules take effect January 2027 and DPH expects the revenue loss from July 2027, with Dorsey chairing the Budget Committee in between.

fail_reasons: check_1_recap: the source is a 556-word candidate questionnaire, and the note reproduces nearly all of its factual content (the $34M reserve, the $90-180M DPH estimate, the $315M citywide projection, the $40M in DPH cuts, the four-month residential wait) plus a paraphrase of Dorsey's actual answer. A reader who reads only the note has the entire piece. The arithmetic framing is genuinely ours and worth keeping. Suggested fix: hold the $34M against the $90-180M contrast and cut the $315M and $40M figures, so the note argues from two numbers instead of five.
